titleEn: When the Water Rises, Up to the Bank!

pages.text: "The rain stopped! Let's find shells!" Pongi splashed through mud by the water. On the bank, Dad, in his overalls, turned the wet boat over to drain it. The canal water was yellow and cloudy.

But the water kept rising. Up to her ankles, then up to her knees. The place where she had found shells disappeared underwater. "Oh? Dad, what's happening to the water?" Pongi looked around, not knowing what to do.
Dad spoke calmly. "The heavy rain is making the water rise. It's all right. Let's go up to the bank." His voice slowed Pongi's heartbeat too. "Yes, Dad!" She held his paw tightly.

Grandpa Goose, the canal keeper in boots, stood by a post on the bank. A line was marked on the post. The water had risen just below it. "When the water reaches this line, everyone goes up to the bank," said Grandpa.

"Shall we try being like Grandpa?" Dad said into Pongi's ear. "When water rises, geese go somewhere high and stretch their necks to look." Pongi stretched her neck and looked. Dad sang, "When the water rises, up to the bank!"

On the bank, Dad counted three steps. "One, when the water reaches the line, up to the bank! Two, hold a grown-up's paw tight! Three, wait on the bank until the water goes down!" Pongi held both paws to her chest. "I can be like a goose too!"

Grandpa opened the water gate. Water rushed out. Pongi held Dad's paw tightly on the bank and watched the line on the post. She called softly, "When the water rises, up to the bank!" She wasn't scared.
The water slowly went down. The line on the post was clear again. "There we are," said Grandpa. Pongi thumped her tail on the bank. "I kept all three rules without crying!"

Pongi tapped the line with her paw. "One, when the water reaches the line, up to the bank! Two, hold a grown-up's paw tight! Three, wait until the water goes down!" The water was far below the line now.

That evening, Dad hugged Pongi tight. "You watched the line right to the end. Well done, Pongi!" When the water rises, she can go up to the bank. In Dad's arms, Pongi smiled. "When the water rises, up to the bank!"
